clue.text: Perks from working in public transport

indicators.note: in places the word for working inside the word for public transport

parts.note: buses are public transport
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Someone praising the fringe benefits of a job driving buses or trains.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonuses are extra payments on top of salary, the kind of extras called perks.

clue.text: Swallowed last of fruit appended to branch

indicators.note: appended to means the letter is added at the end of the branch word

parts.note: a bough is a branch of a tree

indicators.note: last of takes the final letter of fruit

parts.note: the word whose last letter is taken

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit eaten after being joined to a branch.
explanation.walkthrough: Swallowed is meant in its sense of believed, as in swallowing a lie.
explanation.definitionFit: To have bought a story is to have accepted it as true, as swallowed means in the credulous sense.

clue.text: Turning brownish, river shows way of the world

indicators.note: turning means the word is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: tan is a brownish colour
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: A river going brown shows how the world works.
explanation.definitionFit: Nature is the natural order of things, the way the world works.

clue.text: Racing-car brand adding unknown variable to articles shaped with carbon

indicators.note: shaped says the letters are formed into something new

parts.note: x is the usual unknown in algebra
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A toy maker's product put together from parts, variables and carbon.
explanation.walkthrough: Scalextric is a British brand of slot-car racing sets.
explanation.definitionFit: Scalextric is the trade name of a popular model slot-car racing toy.

clue.text: Delightful meal reduced by one penny

indicators.note: reduced by one means a single copy of the letter is taken away

parts.note: supper is an evening meal

explanation.surface: A lovely dinner that cost a penny less.
explanation.definitionFit: Super is informal praise for something excellent or delightful.

clue.text: No cheers for film award? Ran off perplexed

indicators.note: No here means without, so the word for cheers is removed from the award

parts.note: a BAFTA is a British Academy film award
ta is British slang for thanks, i.e. cheers
fled means ran off

explanation.surface: A film-maker, denied applause for a prize, storms out confused.
explanation.walkthrough: BAFTA is the British Academy of Film and Television Arts award; ta (thanks) is British slang matching 'cheers' in its thank-you sense, so BAFTA loses TA to leave BAF.
explanation.definitionFit: Baffled and perplexed are synonyms, both meaning confused or unable to understand.

clue.text: City pub about to welcome Musk, say

parts.note: a bar is a pub

indicators.note: to welcome means the word for about takes in the name

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means about
Elon is the first name of the businessman Musk

explanation.surface: A city bar preparing to receive Elon Musk.
explanation.definitionFit: Barcelona is the Spanish city that is the capital of Catalonia.

clue.text: Start to fetch loose fibrous material

indicators.note: start to takes the opening letter of fetch

parts.note: the word whose first letter is taken
lax means loose or slack

explanation.surface: An instruction to go and get some loose fibre.
explanation.definitionFit: Flax is a plant whose stem fibres are spun into linen.

clue.text: One trying to hear register with French name coming up

parts.note: a list is a register

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: René is a French man's name

explanation.surface: Someone straining to catch a French name read from a register.
explanation.definitionFit: A listener is a person paying attention to sounds, someone making an effort to hear.

clue.text: Soldiers trapped in circular object alien guarded

indicators.note: trapped in means the soldiers are placed inside the other words

parts.note: a disc is a circular object
ET is the film alien
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Soldiers caught in a flying saucer, guarded by an alien.
explanation.definitionFit: A discreet person is careful about what they reveal, which is to be guarded.

clue.text: Difficult rabble not totally extreme

indicators.note: neither word is used in full, so the answer is a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An unruly mob that is hard to handle, yet not quite fanatical.
explanation.definitionFit: Ultra as an adjective or prefix means going beyond the usual, i.e. extreme.

clue.text: Mount mean equine in North America

parts.note: par is the average or mean level

indicators.note: in puts the equine inside the letters for North America

parts.note: N is the compass abbreviation for North
an ass is an equine animal

explanation.surface: Talk of a nasty horse in North America, read as a stingy rider's mount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mount mean equine' reads like a nasty horse to ride; Mount is the definition, a mountain's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Parnassus is a Greek mountain, sacred to Apollo and the Muses.

clue.text: Uncovered part within set not easily obtained

indicators.note: within places the uncovered word inside the word for set

parts.note: to set, like concrete or jelly, is to harden; hardened means set

indicators.note: uncovered means the word loses its outer letters

parts.note: the word whose covering letters are stripped

explanation.surface: Instructions about placing a bare section inside a set, ending with something hard to get.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard-earned describes something gained only through much effort, not easily obtained.

clue.text: Rush drink, first of revelry

parts.note: tea is a drink

indicators.note: first of takes only the opening letter of revelry

parts.note: the word whose first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Someone hurries their drink as the party starts.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear along is to rush or move at great speed.

clue.text: It seems somewhat cheap, parent lying

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A suspicion that a stingy parent is not telling the truth.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparently is used to report what seems to be the case, as 'it seems' does.

clue.text: Sherpa travelling with rest to high region

indicators.note: travelling suggests these words move about and come out in a new order

explanation.surface: A Himalayan guide trekking with time for rest on the way up to great altitude.
explanation.definitionFit: The stratosphere is a layer of the atmosphere well above the clouds, a lofty zone of the sky.

clue.text: We may lose after performing really well

indicators.note: performing suggests these words acting out a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A team fears defeat after playing brilliantly.
explanation.definitionFit: Awesomely is informal for in an amazing way, so very well indeed.

clue.text: One criticised taking in old stray

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: taking in means the criticised word wraps around the letter for old

parts.note: to be slated is to be harshly criticised

explanation.surface: A lone figure is criticised for adopting an old stray animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A stray instance is a lone, isolated one, cut off from the rest.

clue.text: Property secured by trade union involved in acts of arson

indicators.note: involved in places these letters inside the word for acts of arson

parts.note: fires are what arsonists start
x, the multiplication sign, is read as by, as in 3 by 4

explanation.surface: A union caught up in arson attacks on secured property.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is not a link word: it gives X, from dimensions such as 3 x 4.
explanation.definitionFit: Fixtures are items attached to a building, so property fastened in place.

clue.text: Secretly carried off article in bold manner

indicators.note: in places the article inside the words for bold manner

parts.note: spirited means bold
a way is a manner
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Something was stolen, the theft described as daringly done.
explanation.definitionFit: To spirit something away is an idiom for removing it quickly and covertly.

clue.text: President promoting new Republican organiser

indicators.note: promoting moves the letter for new higher up the word

parts.note: Biden is a US President

explanation.surface: A president advancing a new Republican party organiser.
explanation.definitionFit: A binder is a ring folder for keeping papers in order, a desk organiser.

clue.text: Cross empty highway and propose to maintain run

indicators.note: empty removes the inside of highway, leaving its outer letters

parts.note: the word whose outer letters are kept

indicators.note: to maintain means the word for propose holds the letter for run

parts.note: to bid is to propose or offer
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Plans to keep a deserted motorway running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' is the noun meaning a mix of two breeds, not the verb or adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A hybrid is the offspring of two different species or varieties, a cross.

clue.text: Many books in libraries having content cut out

indicators.note: in places the books inside what is left of libraries
the inside of the word is removed, leaving its first and last letters

parts.note: the word whose ends are kept
OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: Libraries gutted of their stock, many books gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Many books' looks like one phrase, but Many alone is the definition and books is OT, the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Lots is an informal quantity word meaning a large number, i.e. many.

clue.text: Agree to embrace old lover, it leads to complication

indicators.note: to embrace means the agreeing word wraps around the old lover and it

parts.note: to comply is to agree or go along
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: Agreeing to hug a former partner, which causes trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Complexity is the state of being intricate, the quality a complication brings.

clue.text: Part of bloomer's soft with delayed rising

definitions.note: the 's is read as is, linking the definition to the wordplay

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for soft

indicators.note: rising in a down clue means the word is read upwards

parts.note: late means delayed

explanation.surface: A soft loaf, a bloomer, slow to rise in the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: A bloomer is a British loaf of bread, but here it is a flower, something that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: A petal is one of the coloured leaves of a flower, a part of a blooming plant.

clue.text: Boring puppet having nothing replaced by you, we hear

indicators.note: replaced by means the letter for nothing is swapped out for the sound of you

parts.note: a doll is a toy figure like a puppet
O is the figure zero, nothing

indicators.note: we hear says the word sounds like a single letter

parts.note: the word you is said aloud and sounds like the letter U

explanation.surface: A dull puppet show improved by replacing an empty part with you.
explanation.definitionFit: Dull and boring are synonyms for something tedious and uninteresting.

clue.text: Turn blue at sea with temperature unstable

indicators.note: at sea means confused or in disarray, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: A sailor turning blue with cold on rough water.
explanation.definitionFit: Turbulent describes something agitated and disordered, hence unstable.

clue.text: Study worm that's completely stripped historic house

indicators.note: both words lose their outer letters, leaving only their middles

parts.note: the word whose outer letters go
the second word whose outer letters go

explanation.surface: A worm laid bare as a specimen in a historic mansion.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tudors were the royal house that ruled England from 1485 to 1603, a dynasty in history.

clue.text: Advertise those involved in police drama

parts.note: DIs are detective inspectors, police officers
a play is a drama

explanation.surface: Promoting a TV crime series and the officers in it.
explanation.walkthrough: DI is the British abbreviation for Detective Inspector, so several of them are DIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To display something is to show it publicly, which is what advertising does.

clue.text: Cut yew and alder neatly piled in sheets

indicators.note: neatly suggests the letters are rearranged into a tidy new order
cut means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: the tree name that is shortened

explanation.surface: Felled yew and alder trees stacked tidily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' trims yew to YE; those letters with ALDER are then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Layered means arranged in stacked strata, one level on another.
